ordering_rationale: Boundaries follow interval normalization, cutting, run geometry, measurement, connected components, recursive tree execution, and synchronized state operations rather than predicate namespaces. All 91 frozen contracts occur exactly once. Independent ready roots are ordered normalization, executor, restricted state interface, cutting, and read-only queries; this prioritizes broad semantic interfaces while keeping restricted progress independent of general adequacy. Hard imports deliberately commit consumers to sealed result packages: normalized algebra/geometry/measure use output invariants; mixed and repeated cuts use primitive cut semantics; components use run geometry; state traces use executor, wrapper and query interfaces. These form an acyclic DAG and are not scheduling-only edges. The recursive executor stays physically together because rotation/removal/pruning interact; separate add/remove providers would risk artificial cycles. Canonical primitive operations instead collaborate across physical theories with reciprocal advisory reuse. Alternatives considered include a single interval theory (too broad), separate primitive executor commands (premature interfaces), and a single refinement theory (would delay static queries and assumption-free wrapper behavior). Definition equations and specification bodies are evidence about semantics, not proofs of the pending specifications. No exact helpers or local proof DAG is imposed; the inspected coalesce.induct fact remains available without committing a proof route. Shared parent context alone creates no generated import. Proof feasibility and availability of shared auxiliary facts remain File Planner questions. Pre-freeze revision: Canonical_Measure now appears immediately after Interval_Normalization as an independent ready root, exposing C0020 to Interval_Measure and Repeated_Cutting. Other relative priorities remain unchanged. Repeated_Cutting now has no hard path through normalization or general merge measure. These two canonical-measure imports commit to a concrete restricted interface, not priority. The executor adequacy split was considered but retained as one package because shared intermediate-state reasoning remains uncertain; successful trace invariants do not themselves require adequacy. No proof-independence claim follows from these definitions.
